title: How Sink Drainage Works: Understanding Traps and Vents
description: Sink drainage relies on a carefully balanced system of gravity, atmospheric pressure, and hydraulic seals. At the core of this system is the trap, typically a curved section of piping located directly beneath the fixture. The trap holds a standing column of water that acts as a vital barrier, preventing sewer gases and unpleasant odors from entering the living space. Downstream of the trap, the drainage path connects to a vent system that introduces air into the pipes, equalizing pressure and preventing siphon action from pulling the trap dry during heavy water discharges.
